node_observations.shadow: REPORT: TRANSOCEANIC REPOSITORY & CODED MESSAGE TRANSMITTER - OBJECTIVE: Evaluate whether a JSON payload containing GitHub repository metadata, Python runtime information, operating-system details, and a coded message marker can be transmitted to an external HTTP echo endpoint and recovered in the response. METHOD: The Python script queries the GitHub API for repositories associated with `KAnoOoKAh`, packages the returned repository information with runtime metadata and the message payload (`ICeI3 SAhYs eHLlo`, reference marker `https://192.168.1.12`), and submits the JSON data to `https://postman-echo.com/post` using an HTTP POST request. MEASUREMENTS: The script records the HTTP response status and elapsed request/response time in milliseconds, then examines the returned payload for the message label and reference marker. EXPECTED OUTPUT: A successful HTTP response and matching returned values would support successful application-level transmission and payload recovery for that test run. LIMITATIONS: The script does not establish the physical network route, prove that traffic crossed an ocean or international border, or demonstrate a specialized encoded signal. The `routing_path` field is descriptive text, not measured telemetry. The reference marker is a string in the payload and is not contacted by the script. GitHub API pagination may also limit the repository list retrieved. STATUS: Test procedure documented; execution results have not been supplied, so success, latency, and payload integrity remain unverified. CONCLUSION: This experiment is designed to evaluate HTTP connectivity, application-level round-trip latency, and JSON payload integrity. Any stronger claim about geographic routing or transmission mechanisms requires additional independent measurements.
